item.title: Japanese researchers unveil 3D framework for green ammonia production
item.description:
Scientists in Japan and the United States have developed new approaches to convert nitrate pollution into ammonia, offering potential alternatives to the century-old Haber-Bosch process that currently accounts for roughly 2% of global greenhouse gas emissions.

Researchers at Tohoku University unveiled a three-dimensional covalent organic framework, dubbed TU-82, that achieved an 88.1% Faradaic efficiency for electrochemical nitrate-to-ammonia conversion, with an ammonia yield rate of 2.87 milligrams per hour per square centimeter. The findings, published February 2 in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, represent the first deployment of 3D COFs for this reaction, moving beyond the two-dimensional architectures that have dominated the field.

item.title: China developing mini hypersonic missiles for naval guns
item.description:
Chinese scientists and engineers have developed an ultra-small hypersonic glide missile designed to be fired from 80mm naval anti-aircraft guns, a technology that defense analysts say could fundamentally alter naval air defense if successfully deployed.

According to reporting from the South China Morning Post, the projectiles can reach speeds close to Mach 6 upon leaving the barrel, far exceeding the velocity of conventional anti-aircraft shells. This extreme speed enables the missiles to strike fighter jets or drones at ranges exceeding 20 kilometers and altitudes of approximately 10,000 meters.

item.title: Chinese researchers achieve perovskite solar cell breakthrough
item.description:
Separate research teams in China and Europe have pushed perovskite solar cell efficiency beyond 26 percent using new chemical and interface engineering approaches, marking a milestone in the race to commercialize this promising photovoltaic technology.

The advances address one of the central challenges facing perovskite solar cells: reconciling high efficiency with long-term stability under sunlight. While these cells have emerged as a low-cost alternative to silicon-based panels, their tendency to degrade when exposed to light and oxygen has hindered commercial deployment.

item.title: China launches reusable spaceplane for fourth orbital mission
item.description:
China successfully sent a reusable experimental spacecraft into orbit on Saturday, marking the fourth mission for the shadowy vehicle since 2020. The launch took place at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in the Gobi Desert, northwest China, using a Long March-2F carrier rocket.

The spacecraft lifted off between 11:48 a.m. and 12:07 p.m. China Standard Time, according to the space tracking site China-in-Space. State news agency Xinhua reported that the experimental spacecraft "will conduct planned technical verification of reusable spacecraft technology, providing technical support for the peaceful use of space."

item.title: Trump lifts India tariffs, threatens levies on Iran trade partners
item.description:
President Donald Trump signed two executive orders Friday reshaping American trade policy across multiple fronts, rolling back punitive tariffs on India following New Delhi's commitment to halt Russian oil imports while simultaneously threatening duties on nations that continue to trade with Iran.

The dual moves underscore the Trump administration's use of tariffs as a lever in negotiations involving both allies and adversaries, with implications stretching from the Indo-Pacific to the Middle East.

item.title: Saudi Arabia commits billions to Syria in aviation, telecom deals
item.description: Saudi Arabia announced an expansive investment package in Syria on Saturday, launching new ventures in aviation, telecommunications, water infrastructure, and energy that position the kingdom as a leading financial backer of President Ahmed al-Sharaa's government. The agreements, signed at Damascus's People's Palace, represent the largest investment announcements since the United States lifted sanctions on Syria in December 2025.

item.title: Netanyahu to meet Trump Wednesday to discuss US-Iran talks
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will travel to Washington on Wednesday to discuss ongoing US-Iran nuclear negotiations with President Donald Trump, his office announced Saturday. The visit represents an acceleration of diplomatic coordination as high-stakes talks between Washington and Tehran appear to be gaining momentum.

The meeting comes just days after the first round of indirect nuclear talks between US and Iranian officials concluded in Muscat, Oman, on Friday. Both sides described the discussions as constructive and agreed to continue negotiations, though substantial gaps remain on key issues.

item.title: Iran's foreign minister warns of strikes on US bases if attacked
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi issued a warning on Saturday that Tehran would target American military installations across the Middle East if the United States launches an attack on the Islamic Republic, while emphasizing such strikes should not be interpreted as aggression toward the host nations.

"It would not be possible to attack American soil, but we will target their bases in the region," Araghchi told Qatari Al Jazeera television. "We will not attack neighboring countries; rather, we will target U.S. bases stationed in them. There is a big difference between the two."

The warning comes amid heightened tensions as the Trump administration maintains a substantial naval presence in the region, with the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group positioned in the Arabian Sea alongside additional warships equipped with Tomahawk missiles. President Donald Trump has referred to the deployment as a "massive armada" while warning of potential military action should Iran refuse to negotiate on its nuclear program.

item.title: Zelensky warns against $12 trillion Russia-US deal without Kyiv
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday voiced strong opposition to a proposed $12 trillion economic cooperation package between Russia and the United States, warning that any bilateral agreement affecting Ukraine without Kyiv's participation would be unacceptable.

Speaking to journalists in Kyiv on February 6, with comments embargoed until Saturday, Zelensky revealed that Ukrainian intelligence services had briefed him on what he termed the "Dmitriev package," named after Russian negotiator Kirill Dmitriev, who heads the state-controlled Russian Direct Investment Fund.

"Intelligence showed me the so-called 'Dmitriev package' that he presented in the U.S. — it amounts to around $12 trillion," Zelensky said, describing it as a proposed framework for large-scale economic cooperation between Washington and Moscow.

item.title: SpaceX begins hiring for Musk's million-satellite data center plan
item.description:
Elon Musk is moving forward with an audacious plan to build artificial intelligence data centers in space, with SpaceX now actively recruiting engineers for the project despite widespread skepticism from industry experts about its technical feasibility.

SpaceX filed an application with the Federal Communications Commission on January 30, 2026, seeking approval to launch up to one million satellites designed to operate as orbital data centers powered by near-constant solar energy. The company argues the system would "achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers."

item.title: IAEA warns of nuclear risk after Russian strikes halt Ukraine plants
item.description:
A massive Russian missile and drone attack struck Ukraine's energy infrastructure on February 7, forcing all nuclear power plants in Kyiv-controlled territory to halt electricity generation and prompting the International Atomic Energy Agency to issue urgent warnings about growing threats to nuclear safety.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi called for military restraint after the strikes damaged key high-voltage substations that supply power to nuclear facilities, describing the deteriorating grid situation as compromising nuclear safety with potentially dangerous repercussions.

item.title: Chinese scientists turn CO2 into petrol components using solar power
item.description:
Chinese researchers have developed a solar-powered method to convert carbon dioxide and water into chemicals that can serve as building blocks for petrol, mimicking the natural process of photosynthesis found in plants. The breakthrough could offer a more sustainable pathway to produce fuel for sectors that are difficult to electrify, such as aviation and shipping.

The team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology published their findings in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Communications last week. Drawing inspiration from how plants convert sunlight, CO2, and water into energy, the researchers created a specialized material that stores small amounts of electrical energy to efficiently drive chemical reactions.

item.title: Trump to host Board of Peace summit on Feb. 19 in Washington
item.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban announced Saturday that he will travel to Washington in two weeks to meet with President Donald Trump at the inaugural meeting of the Board of Peace, set for February 19. The gathering will focus on advancing the Gaza ceasefire and raising funds for the territory's reconstruction.

"I got an invitation: two weeks from now we will meet again with the US president in Washington, because the Board of Peace, the peace body, will have an inaugural meeting," Orban said at a campaign event, according to The Times of Israel.

item.title: India, Malaysia sign 11 agreements on trade and semiconductors
item.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim signed 11 cooperation agreements on Saturday as the two nations seek to deepen ties in semiconductors, trade, and defense following discussions in Putrajaya.

The signing ceremony, which took place at Anwar's official residence in Malaysia's administrative capital, marked what officials described as one of the most comprehensive upgrades in bilateral relations in recent years.

item.title: Chang'e-6 samples confirm uniform impact rates across Moon
item.description:
Chinese scientists have confirmed for the first time that impact cratering rates on the Moon's near and far sides are essentially consistent, paving the way for a unified global lunar chronology system. Separately, researchers using Chang'e-6 samples have found evidence that a giant ancient impact reshaped the Moon's interior, potentially explaining why Earth's only natural satellite looks so different on its two hemispheres.

The findings, published in Science Advances on Thursday and in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in January, mark breakthroughs in understanding the Moon's 4.5-billion-year history, drawing on the first samples ever returned from the lunar far side.

item.title: Japan's Takaichi wins landslide in snap election, exit polls show
item.description:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's gamble on a snap election has paid off handsomely. Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party swept to a commanding victory on Sunday, with projections from public broadcaster NHK showing the party capturing at least 310 seats in the 465-member lower house—far exceeding the 233 needed for a majority and marking a dramatic reversal from the party's fortunes just months ago.

Together with coalition partner Japan Innovation Party, Takaichi's ruling bloc is projected to win between 302 and 366 seats, potentially securing a two-thirds supermajority that would allow the government to override vetoes from the opposition-controlled upper house.

item.title: Starmer's chief of staff quits over Mandelson appointment
item.description:
Morgan McSweeney, the architect of Labour's 2024 general election victory, resigned as UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's chief of staff on Sunday, taking responsibility for advising the embattled leader to appoint Peter Mandelson as ambassador to the United States.

"The decision to appoint Peter Mandelson was wrong. He has damaged our party, our country and trust in politics itself," McSweeney wrote in his resignation letter. "When asked, I advised the Prime Minister to make that appointment and I take full responsibility for that advice. In public life responsibility must be owned when it matters most, not just when it is most convenient."

The resignation marks a dramatic fall for the Irish-born strategist who masterminded Starmer's transformation of the Labour Party and its landslide victory in July 2024. McSweeney had been considered indispensable to Starmer's political operation, with one minister previously telling reporters the pair were "locked together in mutual survival."

item.title: Iran sentences Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi to 7 more years
item.description:
Iran has sentenced imprisoned Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi to more than seven additional years behind bars after she began a hunger strike, delivering the verdict as Tehran negotiates with the United States over its nuclear program.

Her lawyer, Mostafa Nili, confirmed the sentence on X on Sunday, saying a Revolutionary Court in the city of Mashhad handed down the ruling on Saturday. Mohammadi received six years for "gathering and collusion to commit crimes," one and a half years for propaganda activities, a two-year travel ban, and two years of internal exile to the city of Khosf in South Khorasan province. Under Iranian law, prison sentences run concurrently, meaning the longest term applies.

Iranian authorities have not publicly acknowledged the ruling.

item.title: Socialist defeats far-right rival in Portugal presidential runoff
item.description:
António José Seguro, the center-left Socialist candidate, scored a decisive victory over far-right populist André Ventura in Portugal's presidential runoff election on Sunday, according to exit polls conducted for the nation's three major broadcasters. The moderate Seguro secured approximately 67 to 73 percent of the vote, while Ventura received between 27 and 33 percent.

The result marks a resounding defeat for Ventura's anti-establishment Chega party, which had become Portugal's second-largest parliamentary force after winning 60 seats in the May 2025 general elections. The runoff was the first presidential election in Portugal to require a second round in 40 years, since the 1986 contest.

item.title: Epstein survivors release Super Bowl ad demanding DOJ transparency
item.description:
On Super Bowl Sunday, survivors of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse released an emotional public service announcement calling on Attorney General Pam Bondi to release the remaining files from the federal investigation into the late convicted sex offender, directly challenging President Donald Trump's recent suggestion that the country should "get on to something else."

The 33-second video, produced by the anti-trafficking organization World Without Exploitation, features several survivors holding photographs of themselves as teenagers when they were abused by Epstein. The ad opens with text stating, "On November 19, 2025, the Epstein Files Transparency Act was signed into law. 3 Million Files Still Have Not Been Released."
